title: KING: Generating Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios for Robust Imitation via Kinematics Gradients

control_signal.value: Adversarial objective of inducing a collision between background agents and the ego agent under test; the number of adversarial agents (1, 2, 4) is set explicitly.

control_mechanism.value: Gradient-based optimization of adversarial agents' actions, backpropagating through a differentiable kinematic bicycle model (direct path only) in closed-loop simulation.

base_model.value: Kinematic bicycle model as simulator proxy; attacked agents are AIM-BEV and TransFuser imitation policies; rule-based privileged expert solves scenarios for fine-tuning data.

datasets.value: CARLA 0.9.10.1: Town03-Town06 with 80 ego routes for attack evaluation; NEAT validation routes and 82 Town10 dense-traffic intersection routes for driving benchmarks.

metrics.value: Collision rate, time to 50% collision rate, seconds per iteration; CARLA Route Completion, Infraction Score, Driving Score.

controllability_evidence.value: Overall collision rate 82.50% for KING vs 68.33% for CMA-ES and 66.67% for random search; abstract states 20% higher success than black-box optimization.

stated_limitations.value: Using only the direct gradient path introduces an error in gradient estimation. Robustness of agents trained differently (e.g. RL) left to future work.

notes: Not controllable generation in the learned-model sense; it is adversarial scenario optimization against an ego policy. Family set to other.
